quote: In the present study, none of the 10 replications using the RP:P protocol yielded a statistically significant meta-analytic effect size (p < .05)
reason: Primary source identity (Ebersole et al., 2020, DOI 10.1177/2515245920958687) is confirmed via the supplement URL, named organizers (Nosek, Ebersole), and Tables 1-4. However, against prior adjudications (argon and v1) that adopted p = .02 from exploratory Table 4, the target locator ('p.11; Table 3') specifies the confirmatory Table 3 summary, which prints N = 2,811, r = -.04, and 95% CI [-.08, -.01] ('Risen & Gilovich (2008)122.19226.002,811-.04701-.01' / '[.01, .36][-.13, .13][-.08, -.01][-.13, .11]') with no p values. Table 3 and exploratory Table 4 (Mathur & VanderWeele, 2020 meta-analyses) are distinct models whose estimates, CIs, and p values diverge across studies (e.g., Risen & Gilovich revised CI [-.13, .11] in Table 3 vs. [-.18, .16] in Table 4; narrative revised-protocol p values .009 and .005 vs. Table 4 .006 and .008), so k = 1 and rounded r/CI agreement do not establish analytical equivalence for Table 4's 'RP:P protocol1-.04 [-.08, -.01].020.02.95000'. Furthermore, although Table 3's CI [-.08, -.01] excludes zero in the negative direction (showing FReD's coding note 'Table 3 ML5:RP:P Protocol CI includes 0' misread the table), the confirmatory Results introducing Table 3 and the exploratory/Discussion narratives explicitly state that none of the 10 RP:P protocols yielded p < .05; with pval_tails_r null and footnote 5 absent from the parsed text, the source does not resolve whether the Table 3 test used a directional hypothesis or reflects an internal source inconsistency between the negative CI and the 'none ... (p < .05)' statements, leaving both exact p = .02 and the shipped/opposite bounds (> 0.05 vs. < 0.05) undeterminable.
